subproblem.title: Simon submanifolds are locally compact in closed-ball form
subproblem.statement: Let n, N ∈ ℕ, r ∈ ℕ∞ and M ⊆ ℝᴺ (ℝᵈ := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) an n-dimensional C^r Simon submanifold, i.e. Chapter02.IsSimonSubmanifold (E := ℝⁿ) r M. Then for every y ∈ M and every open O ⊆ ℝᴺ with y ∈ O there is a real ρ > 0 such that the closed ball B̄(y, ρ) (Metric.closedBall y ρ) is contained in O and M ∩ B̄(y, ρ) is compact.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n N : ℕ) (r : ℕ∞) (M : Set (Rn N)), Chapter02.IsSimonSubmanifold (E := Rn n) r M → ∀ y ∈ M, ∀ O : Set (Rn N), IsOpen O → y ∈ O → ∃ ρ : ℝ, 0 < ρ ∧ closedBall y ρ ⊆ O ∧ IsCompact (M ∩ closedBall y ρ)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Notation: ℝᵈ := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d). B(y, ε) is the open ball and B̄(y, ρ) = Metric.closedBall y ρ the closed ball.
This is step 3 of the parent proof ("M ∩ S = ψ(V ∩ ψ⁻¹(S)) is compact: relative properness, continuity of ψ on V, W ∩ M = ψ(V)"), stated for an arbitrary point and an arbitrary open neighbourhood.

1. Let y ∈ M and let O ⊆ ℝᴺ be open with y ∈ O. By the second conjunct of IsSimonSubmanifold, there are V ⊆ ℝⁿ, W ⊆ ℝᴺ and ψ : ℝⁿ → ℝᴺ with y ∈ W and IsSimonLocalRepresentation r M V W ψ. That is, V and W are open, ψ is C^r on V, ψ is injective on V, ψ(V) = W ∩ M, ψ is proper relative to (V, W), and Dψ(x) is injective for x ∈ V. Relative properness (IsProperOnInto ψ V W) means V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) is compact for every compact K ⊆ W. Only openness of W, ContDiffOn of ψ on V, the image identity ψ(V) = W ∩ M and relative properness are used below.
2. O ∩ W is open, as an intersection of two open sets, and contains y. By Metric.isOpen_iff there is ε > 0 with B(y, ε) ⊆ O ∩ W. Put ρ := ε/2 > 0. Since ρ < ε, B̄(y, ρ) ⊆ B(y, ε) ⊆ O ∩ W (closedBall_subset_ball). In particular B̄(y, ρ) ⊆ O and B̄(y, ρ) ⊆ W.
3. Claim: M ∩ B̄(y, ρ) = ψ(V ∩ ψ⁻¹(B̄(y, ρ))).
   (⊆) Let z ∈ M ∩ B̄(y, ρ). By step 2, z ∈ W, so z ∈ W ∩ M = ψ(V). Write z = ψ(x) with x ∈ V. Then ψ(x) = z ∈ B̄(y, ρ), so x ∈ V ∩ ψ⁻¹(B̄(y, ρ)) and z = ψ(x) lies in the right-hand side.
   (⊇) Let x ∈ V with ψ(x) ∈ B̄(y, ρ). Then ψ(x) ∈ ψ(V) = W ∩ M ⊆ M, so ψ(x) ∈ M ∩ B̄(y, ρ).
4. B̄(y, ρ) is compact, since closed balls of the finite-dimensional (proper) space ℝᴺ are compact (isCompact_closedBall). Also B̄(y, ρ) ⊆ W by step 2. So by relative properness, K₀ := V ∩ ψ⁻¹(B̄(y, ρ)) is compact.
5. ψ is C^r on V, hence continuous on V (ContDiffOn.continuousOn), hence continuous on K₀ ⊆ V. The image of a compact set under a map continuous on that set is compact (IsCompact.image_of_continuousOn), so ψ(K₀) is compact. By step 3, M ∩ B̄(y, ρ) = ψ(K₀), so M ∩ B̄(y, ρ) is compact.
6. Thus 0 < ρ, B̄(y, ρ) ⊆ O (step 2) and M ∩ B̄(y, ρ) is compact (step 5), which is the claim. ∎
proof_key_steps: Take a chart (V, W, ψ) of M with y ∈ W, and choose ρ > 0 with B̄(y, ρ) ⊆ O ∩ W, e.g. half the radius of an open ball inside O ∩ W.
Since B̄(y, ρ) ⊆ W and ψ(V) = W ∩ M, M ∩ B̄(y, ρ) = ψ(V ∩ ψ⁻¹(B̄(y, ρ))).
B̄(y, ρ) is a compact subset of W, so relative properness makes V ∩ ψ⁻¹(B̄(y, ρ)) compact.
ψ is continuous on V, so the image M ∩ B̄(y, ρ) is compact.

audit.reason: The one-line proposition exactly matches all prose hypotheses and conclusions. The proof correctly chooses a closed ball inside the open chart target, establishes the image/preimage identity in both directions, applies relative properness, and takes a continuous image of the compact preimage. It needs no closedness assumption on M and no parent or sibling theorem. The bare name is unreserved, and the complete proof is sufficient for direct formalization.
